transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

That pattern most often means the dryer is overheating: its safety cut-out stops it after a while, then resets once it has cooled. With a vented dryer, restricted airflow from fluff or the hose is the usual reason. A failing thermostat/thermal cut-out is possible, but only after the airflow is proved clear. 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Remove and thoroughly clean the lint filter, including fluff around its housing. If it is packed with fluff, that strongly supports overheating from poor airflow.
2. Check the hose from dryer to window: it should be as short and straight as practical, with no squash, sharp bends, water in it or fluff blockage. The hose end must not be trapped against the window or covered by a grille/cloth. Clear or reposition it if needed.
3. Check the load: avoid one small item and avoid overfilling the drum; use a normal-sized load for the next test.
4. After cleaning/straightening the airflow path, run a normal programme while staying nearby. If it now runs continuously, airflow was the cause. If it still cuts out at around the same point despite a clean filter and clear hose, the thermostat/thermal cut-out or blower fan needs an engineer to inspect. If there is any burning-lint smell, smoke, scorching, or the casing becomes exceptionally hot, stop using it, unplug it and arrange a repair rather than testing it again.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok did the filter, its clean, i clean it every time. the hose is crushed behind the dryer tho, i pushed it back further recently. also the cabinet gets really hot before it stops

The crushed hose is very likely the cause. Pushing the dryer further back has restricted the outlet airflow; heat then builds up, the cabinet gets very hot and the overheat protection cuts the dryer out until it cools. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Pull the dryer forward and reroute or replace the hose so it is not flattened, sharply bent or trapped behind the machine. Keep it as short and straight as reasonably possible, and leave enough space behind the dryer that it cannot squash again.
2. Check the full hose length and the window end for fluff or anything covering the outlet.
3. Only once that is sorted, run a normal load while nearby. It should expel a strong flow of warm air and should not become exceptionally hot or stop after about 10 minutes. Do not use it with the hose crushed. If it still overheats or cuts out with a free, clear hose, stop using it and arrange an engineer: the blower fan, thermostat or thermal cut-out then needs checking rather than simply fitting another cut-out.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
ok will pull it out and sort the hose. should i run it with the hose off the window first to check? its a rented flat, dryer is the landlords

No — don’t run it with the hose simply off the window and blowing into the flat. A vented dryer needs to discharge its hot, damp air outside; venting indoors can cause condensation and leaves lint in the room. Pull it forward with it switched off and unplugged, then arrange the hose so it reaches out of the window without being crushed, sharply bent or trapped. If the hose is damaged or remains flattened, report that to the landlord/agent rather than altering the dryer itself. Then do one supervised normal-load test. There should be a clear, warm airflow at the outdoor end and it should not become exceptionally hot or stop after roughly 10 minutes. If it still cuts out once the hose is free and venting outdoors, stop using it and ask the landlord to arrange an engineer: the blower fan, thermostat or thermal cut-out will need checking.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
